title: Compare Simple Forecast Models

  sine wave time series with added noise. The evaluation uses Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) as primary
  metrics to quantify predictive accuracy. The `eval.py` script generates the synthetic data, calculates predictions for both

  errors. The naive forecast generally exhibited lower MSE and MAE on this specific synthetic series, suggesting its immediate
  adaptation to the last observed value was more effective than the smoothing effect of the 3-point moving average for this
  particular dataset characteristics.

import json, os

def load_data():

        import urllib.request
        with urllib.request.urlopen(GITHUB_DATA_URL) as response:

    raise FileNotFoundError("Could not load mini_demo_data.json")

For each point, the prediction is the average of the three preceding true values. Edge cases for the first few points are handled separately.\"\n            ]\n        },\n        {\n            \"cell_type\": \"code\",\n            \"execution_count\": None,\n            \"metadata\": {},\n            \"outputs\": [],\n            \"source\": [\n                \"moving_avg_predictions = []\\n\",\n                \"moving_avg_predictions.append(true_values[0]) # For the first point, no prior data. These values are set to minimal levels for a quick demonstration.\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"code\",\n   \"execution_count\": null,\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"outputs\": [],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"# Tunable parameters\\n\",\n    \"SERIES_LENGTH = 20  # Number of points in the synthetic time series (original: 20)\\n\",\n    \"NOISE_STD_DEV = 0.1 # Standard deviation of the noise added to the sine wave (original: 0.1)\\n\",\n    \"RANDOM_SEED = 42    # Random seed for reproducibility\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"## Processing\\n\",\n    \"### Generate Synthetic Time Series Data\\n\",\n    \"A synthetic sine wave time series with added Gaussian noise is generated to simulate input data for the forecasting models.\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"code\",\n   \"execution_count\": null,\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"outputs\": [],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"np.random.seed(RANDOM_SEED)\\n\",\n    \"true_values = np.sin(np.linspace(0, 3 * np.pi, SERIES_LENGTH)) + np.random.normal(0, NOISE_STD_DEV, SERIES_LENGTH)\\n\",\n    \"logger.info(\\\"Generated synthetic time series of length {}.\\\".format(SERIES_LENGTH))\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"### Generate Predictions: 3-point Moving Average\\n\",\n    \"This section implements a 3-point moving average forecasting model. For each point, the prediction is the average of the three preceding true values. Edge cases for the first few points are handled separately.\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"code\",\n   \"execution_count\": null,\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"outputs\": [],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"moving_avg_predictions = []\\n\",\n    \"moving_avg_predictions.append(true_values[0]) # For the first point, no prior data. Use the true value itself\\n\",\n    \"if SERIES_LENGTH > 1:\\n\",\n    \"    moving_avg_predictions.append(true_values[0]) # For the second point, only one prior data point. Use the first true value.\\n\",\n    \"if SERIES_LENGTH > 2:\\n\",\n    \"    moving_avg_predictions.append(np.mean(true_values[0:2])) # For the third point, two prior data points. For the very first point, it uses its own true value.\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"code\",\n   \"execution_count\": null,\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"outputs\": [],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"naive_predictions = [true_values[max(0, i-1)] for i in range(SERIES_LENGTH)]\\n\",\n    \"naive_predictions = np.array(naive_predictions)\\n\",\n    \"logger.info(\\\"Generated naive last-value forecast predictions.\\\")\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"### Calculate Evaluation Metrics\\n\",\n    \"Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) are calculated for both forecasting models by comparing their predictions against the true values of the synthetic time series.\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"code\",\n   \"execution_count\": null,\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"outputs\": [],\n   \"source\": [\n    \"metrics = {}\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"# 3-point moving average\\n\",\n    \"mse_ma = mean_squared_error(true_values, moving_avg_predictions)\\n\",\n    \"mae_ma = mean_absolute_error(true_values, moving_avg_predictions)\\n\",\n    \"metrics[\\\"moving_average\\\"] = {\\\"MSE\\\": mse_ma, \\\"MAE\\\": mae_ma}\\n\",\n    \"logger.info(\\\"Moving Average - MSE: {:.4f}, MAE: {:.4f}\\\".format(mse_ma, mae_ma))\\n\",\n    \"\\n\",\n    \"# Naive last-value forecast\\n\",\n    \"mse_naive = mean_squared_error(true_values, naive_predictions)\\n\",\n    \"mae_naive = mean_absolute_error(true_values, naive_predictions)\\n\",\n    \"metrics[\\\"naive_forecast\\\"] = {\\\"MSE\\\": mse_naive, \\\"MAE\\\": mae_naive}\\n\",\n    \"logger.info(\\\"Naive Forecast - MSE: {:.4f}, MAE: {:.4f}\\\".format(mse_naive, mae_naive))\"\n   ]\n  },\n  {\n   \"cell_type\": \"markdown\",\n   \"metadata\": {},\n   \"source\": [\n    \"## Results\\n\",\n    \"### Summary and Visualization\\n\",\n    \"This section presents the aggregated evaluation metrics and visualizes the true values alongside the predictions from both models.
